channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Lectures in History
channel.desc: Washington University hosts a series of lectures called 1776: Then and Now. This lecture examines the international context of the American Revolution.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Ceasefire
channel.desc: Thomas Jefferson (Bill Barker) and John Adams (Peyton Dixon) join host Dasha Burns to trace their extraordinary journey from co-authors of American independence, to political adversaries, to reconciled friends.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: America 250
channel.desc: Former President Bill Clinton reflects on the life and legacy of Theodore Roosevelt, America's 26th president (1901-09). His essay is part of a project called In Pursuit, commissioned to mark America's 250th birthday in 2026.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: America 250
channel.desc: George Washington (portrayed by Dan Shippey) and Ben Franklin (portrayed by Mark Skousen) talk about the 250th anniversary of American independence.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: America 250
channel.desc: Stanford University constitutional scholar Jonathan Gienapp revisits the debates that engaged the Founders as they drafted the Constitution.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Historian Annette Gordon Reed
channel.desc: The George Washington Presidential Library hosts a summit on women's leadership in preserving history.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: The Civil War
channel.desc: Virginia Center for Civil War Studies at Virginia Tech hosts a conference on Civil War innovations.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: The Presidency
channel.desc: Historian H.W. Brands discusses his book American Patriarch, which looks at George Washington and how he became known as the Father of His Country.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: C-SPAN Visits the 1876 Bartholdi Fountain at 150 Years
channel.desc: The Fountain of Light and Water, also known as the Bartholdi Fountain, was created for the Centennial Exposition in Philadelphia in 1876, and is located at the U.S. Botanic Garden in Washington, D.C.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: 2025 Library of Congress Stradivari Concert
channel.desc: The Library of Congress highlights its collection of Stradivarius instruments with a concert held at the Library's Coolidge Auditorium in Washington, D.C. This video was provided by the Library of Congress.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: C-SPAN Tours the Kentucky Derby Museum
channel.desc: C-SPAN tours the Kentucky Derby Museum in Louisville, which details its 150+ year horse racing tradition and its place in American history.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: C-SPAN Tours the Go-Go Museum in Washington, D.C.
channel.desc: C-SPAN tours the Go-Go Museum and hears the history of Washington, D.C.'s homegrown music genre with roots in the cultural and social movements of the mid-1960s to late-1970s.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: America 250
channel.desc: Chief Justice of the United States John Roberts reflects on the life and legacy of William Howard Taft, America's 27th president (1909-13). His essay is part of a project called In Pursuit, commissioned to mark America's 250th birthday in 2026.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: America 250
channel.desc: John Bridgeland, founder and CEO of the organization More Perfect, reflects on the life and legacy of First Lady Helen Taft (1909-13). His essay is part of a project called In Pursuit, commissioned by More Perfect to mark America's 250th birthday.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: America 250
channel.desc: Social entrepreneur Andrew Mangino reflects on the life and legacy of First Lady Frances Cleveland (1886-89, 1893-97). His essay is part of a project called In Pursuit, commissioned to mark America's 250th birthday in 2026.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Lectures in History
channel.desc: The October 2002 speech by George W. Bush making the case for military action in Iraq is the topic of a class taught by University of Kansas political communication professor Robert Rowland.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: American History TV
channel.desc: Airing weekends, "American History TV" offers programming about people and events that document the American story, geared toward history aficionados. Shows that air under the "American History TV" banner cover the history of the nation, from its founding in the 18th century through modern times. Topics covered include the Civil War, presidents and the exploration of historical sites.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: The Presidency
channel.desc: Clifton Truman Daniel, grandson of First Lady Bess Truman (1945-53), joins historians to discuss her life and legacy. The Truman Little White House in Key West hosts this event.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: McCarthyism and the 1950s Red Scare
channel.desc: Historian Beverly Gage discusses the 1950s Red Scare with family members of individuals targeted during the hunt for communists led by Sen. Joseph McCarthy (R-WI.).

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: C-SPAN Tours the Muhammad Ali Center
channel.desc: C-SPAN tours the Muhammad Ali Center in Louisville, Kentucky, to learn about the life and legacy of the heavyweight boxer and global activist.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: America 250
channel.desc: Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia hosts a tour of gravesites and memorials connected to the Revolutionary War.

channel.title: America 250

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Dennis Prager, if There Is No God
channel.desc: Joel Alperson, assistant to Dennis Prager, talks about Mr. Prager's book on the battle between religious morality and secularism. Mr. Prager, who has been paralyzed from the neck down since 2024, provides a video statement.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Ben Rhodes, All We Say
channel.desc: Former Obama Administration speechwriter Ben Rhodes discusses American identity and the history of the country through fifteen speeches dating from the earliest days of the United States to the 21st century.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Q & A
channel.desc: Former Space Shuttle Launch Director Mike Leinbach talks about the 2003 Space Shuttle Columbia disaster that took the lives of the seven astronauts on board. Columbia disintegrated over Texas and Louisiana upon re-entering Earth's atmosphere.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Elise Stefanik, Poisoned Ivies
channel.desc: Rep. Elise Stefanik (R-NY) argues that elite universities in America have embraced a culture of antisemitism, leftist groupthink, and censorship.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Sen. Raphael Warnock D-GA, The Crooked Places Made Straight
channel.desc: Georgia Senator Rev. Raphael Warnock sits down with theologians inside Washington National Cathedral's nave to talk about the ills that, he argues, burden American society.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Max Nikias, American Trojan
channel.desc: Former University of Southern California president Max Nikias talks about his life and leadership at the Los Angeles-based institution.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Melissa Murray, The U.S. Constitution
channel.desc: Former Attorney General Eric Holder interviews law professor and podcast host Melissa Murray about her guide on how to read and understand the U.S. Constitution.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: America's Book Club
channel.desc: Bestselling presidential historian Michael Beschloss joins David M. Rubenstein to discuss broad swaths of American history, including the Revolutionary War era, the Civil War, as well as major events of the 20th century.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: America's Book Club
channel.desc: Bestselling author Ben Mezrich joins David M. Rubenstein to discuss his writing career and how several of his books have been adapted into major Hollywood films, including The Social Network and 21.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: America's Book Club
channel.desc: Bestselling Mary Todd Lincoln biographer Lois Romano joins David M. Rubenstein at Ford's Theatre to discuss Lincoln's early life, time in the White House and mental health.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: America's Book Club
channel.desc: Former Reagan administration official Linda Chavez joins David M. Rubenstein to discuss her career in public service and her works of fiction and nonfiction.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: America's Book Club
channel.desc: Pulitzer Prize winner Jon Meacham joins David M. Rubenstein to discuss his biographies of Thomas Jefferson, Andrew Jackson, and George H.W. Bush, and his upcoming book on Dwight Eisenhower.[(96057)]

channel.title: Book TV
channel.desc: This long-running staple of the C-SPAN2 weekend schedule helps expand the channel's programming beyond politics. Most episodes of "Book TV" feature discussions with authors of nonfiction books, usually in the form of interviews, lectures or seminars. The series sometimes includes coverage of major book fairs and festivals. Some of the notable names who have appeared on the show include David Mamet and Tom Clancy.
